page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for compute-heavy and memory-intensive workloads. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor featuring 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 180.0 GB of system memory, yielding 11.25 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it features a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in large language model (LLM) inference tasks. For a small 135M model, it achieves prompt processing speeds of 13,631.52 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 610.8 tokens per second. With a medium 7B model, prompt processing reaches 6,293.73 tokens per second and text generation reaches 153.1 tokens per second, both placing in the top tier of tested configurations. CPU performance is solid, with a PassMark CPU score of 40,930.36 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 34,834.61. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is highly efficient at 15.59 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 238.14 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a balanced resource density by pairing a high-capacity 48 GB VRAM GPU with a substantial 180 GB system memory allocation and fast NVMe storage. This configuration mitigates potential bottlenecks during large-scale data transfers between system RAM and GPU memory. The server is highly suited for workloads such as LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, and high-throughput database operations.
